description: eGov Phase 1 - PhilHealth Integration - Premium calculator based on 2026 PhilHealth rates and mock coverage verification.
steps: Create lib/services/egov/philhealth_service.dart with calculateMonthlyPremium(monthlySalary) method that returns PhilHealth premium based on 2026 rates: 5% of monthly basic salary (max ₱5,000 contribution = ₱100,000 salary cap), split 50-50 between employer and employee for employed, or full 5% for self-employed/voluntary

Add premium breakdown helper: getPremiumBreakdown(monthlySalary, employmentType) returns object with {totalPremium, employeeShare, employerShare, isMaxCap} where employmentType is 'employed', 'self-employed', or 'voluntary'

Enhance existing lib/screens/gov_contributions_screen.dart (from v3.2.0) to add PhilHealth calculator tab: input for monthly salary and employment type dropdown, result card showing premium breakdown with color-coded employee vs employer shares

Add mock coverage verification to philhealth_service.dart: generateMockCoverageInfo() returns object with {isActive: true, membershipType: 'Employed', lastContribution: 'Oct 2026', availableBenefits: ['Inpatient', 'Outpatient', 'Z Benefits', 'Maternity Care']}
Add coverage verification card to PhilHealth section showing mock active status, last contribution date, and list of available benefits with info buttons explaining each benefit type
Add info button explaining PhilHealth contribution rates, premium caps, and how to verify real coverage at philhealth.gov.ph portal
acceptance_criteria: Premium calculator correctly computes 5% of monthly salary up to ₱5,000 max contribution
Premium breakdown differentiates between employed (50-50 split) and self-employed (100% member pays)
Calculator shows when max cap is reached (salary ≥₱100,000)
Mock coverage verification displays active status and available benefits
Info buttons explain PhilHealth rates and link to official portal
Integration with existing gov_contributions_screen.dart maintains backward compatibility
verification: Test scenario 1: Enter ₱30,000 salary as 'Employed' → premium shows ₱1,500 total (₱750 employee + ₱750 employer)
Test scenario 2: Enter ₱150,000 salary → premium capped at ₱5,000 total with warning 'Max contribution reached'
Test scenario 3: Enter ₱20,000 as 'Self-Employed' → premium shows ₱1,000 total (100% member pays)
Test scenario 4: Mock coverage card displays 'Active' status with 4 benefit categories listed
Test scenario 5: Existing gov_contributions_screen.dart YTD totals still work correctly after adding PhilHealth tab
